description: Rename a secret server-side without exposing plaintext. Reads value+metadata under old_key, writes under new_key, deletes old_key. Use instead of retrieve+store+delete when the plaintext must not cross the process boundary (e.g., MCP / coding-agent contexts).
embedding_description: Vault: rename a secret server-side without exposing plaintext. Moves credential / password / OAuth client_secret / API key / refresh/bearer token from one vault key to another, preserving value + version/tags/metadata. Plaintext never leaves the vault — callers see only key identifiers. Use instead of retrieve+store+delete when round trip would leak plaintext into agent transcript / MCP log.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Confirmation that secret was renamed from old_key to new_key. Contains old_key, new_key, and message (status). NEVER contains secret values.
result_processor_customizations.output_action_guidance: Determine the appropriate next action based on the context and action result.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Renames a secret server-side. Reads value+metadata under old_key, writes under new_key, deletes old_key — atomic within the vault process.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: VaultLocked: Vault must be unlocked before renaming secrets. KeyNotFound: No secret exists with old_key. KeyAlreadyExists: A secret already exists under new_key — refuse to overwrite. AccessDenied: Caller principal lacks operator privileges (rename is operator-only).
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: For VaultLocked: Prompt user to unlock vault first. For KeyNotFound: Verify old_key spelling; the secret may already have been renamed in a prior cycle. For KeyAlreadyExists: Either delete the new_key target first or pick a fresh target. For AccessDenied: Re-issue from an operator-principal context.
